title: Entanglement spectrum and magic in higher-dimensional free fermionic systems
authors: Beatrice Magni, Daniele Iannotti, Riccardo Travaglino
abstract: We study fermionic non-local magic in higher-dimensional free-fermion systems through the lens of the entanglement spectrum. For translationally invariant Gaussian states in strip geometries, dimensional reduction maps the problem to independent lower-dimensional momentum sectors, leading in two dimensions to a multiplicative logarithmic violation of the boundary law analogous to Gioev-Klich-Widom scaling. We further show that the second Rényi fermionic non-local magic is bounded by the capacity of entanglement and introduce an entanglement-temperature deformation that probes the low-energy structure of the entanglement Hamiltonian. Applied to the matter-Majorana sector of the Kitaev model, this response is exponentially suppressed in the Abelian phase and algebraic in the non-Abelian phase, where its ratio with the capacity approaches a universal constant. Out of equilibrium, we extend the quasi-particle description to fermionic non-local magic in higher-dimensional quenches and show that random Gaussian circuits exhibit diffusive spreading in two spatial dimensions.
summary: This work explores fermionic non-local magic in free-fermion systems using the entanglement spectrum as a diagnostic tool. It derives scaling laws for FNL in various geometries and applies these tools to the Kitaev model, showing phase-dependent behavior. Furthermore, it analyzes the time evolution of entanglement measures under random quantum circuits, confirming diffusive dynamics in higher dimensions.
main_problem: The paper investigates fermionic non-local magic (FNL) in higher-dimensional free-fermion systems, relating it to the entanglement spectrum and its behavior under various conditions.
main_result: The study establishes specific scaling laws for FNL in 2D strip geometries and shows that the entanglement-temperature deformation of FNL exhibits distinct behavior (exponential vs. algebraic) in Abelian versus non-Abelian phases of the Kitaev model.
method: The analysis heavily relies on dimensional reduction techniques applied to Gaussian states, utilizing the entanglement spectrum and comparing FNL to other entanglement measures like the capacity of entanglement.
model_or_system: The primary models are higher-dimensional free-fermion systems, analyzed using Gaussian states, and specifically applied to the matter-Majorana sector of the Kitaev model.
key_observables: Fermionic Non-local Magic (FNL), Entanglement Spectrum, Capacity of Entanglement, and the ensemble-averaged squared Majorana weight.
important_parameters: Dimensionality (2D, higher-D), temperature ($T_E$), and system sizes ($\ell, L_y$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the free-fermion Gaussian state setting, allowing for closed spectral expressions, and often employs continuum limits and Gaussian approximations for dynamics.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the dimensional reduction of FNL for a pure Gaussian state in 2D via momentum block decomposition. Figure 10 compares entanglement entropies in random Clifford Gaussian circuits, showing diffusive growth.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing FNL in static, translationally invariant states (strip geometries, Kitaev model) to studying its out-of-equilibrium dynamics under random quantum gates (quenches/circuits), culminating in diffusive spreading results.
why_interesting: The connection between entanglement measures (like FNL) and spectral properties, especially how these quantities reveal underlying topological phases (Abelian vs. non-Abelian) in condensed matter models, is highly relevant to understanding quantum phases of matter.
